concept.name: Term structure
concept.definition: The relationship between the prices (or yields) of contracts on the same underlying asset and their times to maturity or delivery. In futures markets it is synonymous with the futures curve; in rates markets it refers to the yield curve across maturities.
concept.intuition: It answers the question: how does price change purely as a function of when delivery or maturity occurs, holding the asset itself constant?
concept.mechanics: Extracted by holding the underlying constant and varying only the maturity dimension: for commodity futures, the sequence of contract-month prices; for interest rates, yields across maturities. The slope and curvature of the term structure drive roll yield, calendar-spread pricing, and steepener/flattener views.
concept.failure_modes: Term structure mixes expectations with carrying costs, storage, convenience yield, and risk premia, so reading it as a pure forecast of future spot prices is invalid. In thinly traded maturities the observed structure can be distorted by illiquidity.
concept.misconceptions: It is often assumed the term structure is stable or slowly mean-reverting; in practice it can invert within days on supply shocks (e.g., pipeline outages flipping crude from contango to backwardation).
concept.example: Soybean futures show November at $12.10, January at $12.25, and March at $12.35 per bushel: this rising term structure reflects storage and financing costs of carrying beans from harvest into spring.

citations.source: CME Group, CME Institute: What is Contango and Backwardation
